clue.text: Grab at a few bars?

definitions.meaning: a short fragment of a tune, a few bars of music

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden grasp is a seizure, and a brief musical fragment is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Napoleon's adversary wasn't a patch on him? Not true!

definitions.text: Napoleon's adversary wasn't a patch on him? Not true!

parts.words: Napoleon's adversary wasn't a patch on him? Not true!
parts.note: the British admiral who fought Napoleon's fleets famously wore a patch over an eye, so the idiom 'not a patch on' is denied literally

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a rival of Napoleon, swiftly contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a patch on' means inferior to; the clue denies it because the admiral who beat the French at Trafalgar is pictured with an eye patch on him.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral of Trafalgar was Napoleon's great naval opponent, popularly pictured wearing an eye patch.

clue.text: Chief has to lead a fool

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
a nana is British slang for a silly person

explanation.surface: A boss is obliged to lead an idiot around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a verb but is the metal, symbol PB. NANA is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the person in charge, the boss at the top of the pile.

clue.text: Dance with alcohol, a game of balance

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
Scotch is whisky, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A dance with a drink in hand becomes a test of staying upright.
explanation.walkthrough: HOP is an old word for an informal dance; the children's game involves hopping between chalked squares on one leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime where players hop on one leg between squares, so keeping steady is essential.

clue.text: Seek to inspire a bore to produce work of art

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the word for seek takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to seek is to try
a bore, a tiresome person, is a pest

explanation.surface: Someone tries to motivate a tedious person into creating art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspire' is used in its literal sense of breathing in, and 'bore' is a tiresome person rather than a drill or a dull talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall hanging depicting scenes is a classic example of decorative art.

clue.text: Destructive force ruined a party

parts.note: something torn is damaged or ruined
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A violent force wrecked a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' looks like an anagram signal but gives TORN; DO is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm that flattens buildings in its path.

clue.text: Assume one sent?

annotationWithheld.why: Assume one sent? (5): POSIT is I (one) inside POST (sent), but no clue word signals the container; the only parse needs an implied indicator

clue.text: Fill with things

definitions.meaning: an informal word for possessions or miscellaneous items

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cram full; as a noun it is a casual term for belongings or general matter.

clue.text: Something worn, from Croatian translation

indicators.note: translation is taken as turning the word into a different form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garment's name appears when a Croatian word is rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation' is the anagram signal: the letters of CROATIAN rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat is an item of clothing put on over other garments.

clue.text: Bird consuming semi-liquid food, something sticky

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: a flyer, something that flies, stands for a bird
pap is soft, mushy food for babies or invalids

explanation.surface: A bird eating mush ends up stuck to something gummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consuming' puts the baby food inside the word for a bird; 'something sticky' is the definition, not the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gummed paper hung up to trap insects, which is coated in adhesive.

clue.text: Slow sheep caught by James in carry-on?

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the sheep sits within the actor's first name

parts.note: Sid James was a star of the British Carry On comedy films
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A dim sheep is collared by an actor in some comic antics.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were a long series of bawdy British comedies; Sid James starred in many. 'Caught by' puts the ram inside his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow in the sense of dull-witted or lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Doctor has bag containing one's work of art

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the bag wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
I is the Roman numeral for one; the possessive is ignored

explanation.surface: A doctor carries a bag holding his own artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) then SAC holding I.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture assembled from small pieces of coloured tile or glass is a form of decorative art.

clue.text: Find some transport cafe, travelling back

indicators.note: travelling back means the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
some means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Locate a roadside diner while driving home.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters TCAFETRA run through 'transporT CAFE, TRAvelling'; 'back' turns them round. A transport cafe is a British roadside diner for lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaeological discovery, an object dug up, is an example of a man-made object.

clue.text: Either way, original sinner

indicators.note: either way means it reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, the first wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first woman ate the forbidden fruit, committing original sin.

clue.text: Another chance to see OAP certainly sozzled… (6,6) 18…the bar's early to throw out the curse of the drunk driver

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A pensioner, very drunk, gets a second look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sozzled' (British slang for drunk) rearranges OAP CERTAINLY; OAP is old-age pensioner. The ellipsis joins this clue to 18-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A televised repeat of a moment of sport, giving viewers a second look.

clue.text: Scent rising feeling of wonder entering list

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a roster is a list of names or duties

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: A perfume climbing a ranking prompts amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns the feeling of wonder upside down in this down clue, giving EWA; 'entering' puts that inside the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant liquid distilled from petals, used as a perfume and flavouring.

clue.text: A force kept within safe limit

indicators.note: kept within means held inside, so the safe encloses the other letters

parts.note: peter is criminal slang for a safe
to ram is to force

explanation.surface: Keeping a force inside a secure boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept within' puts A and the force inside the safe; 'safe' looks like an adjective describing 'limit' but is criminal slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary or constraint, a set bound within which something must operate.

clue.text: Are possibly a thousand involved in fight to escape?

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so these letters go into the fight

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the word may be arranged differently

parts.note: K is short for a thousand

explanation.surface: Could a thousand people join a scrap to get free?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the letters of 'Are' to give REA; 'involved in' puts that and the thousand inside the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbreak is an escape from prison, often by force.

clue.text: . the bar's early to throw out the curse of the drunk driver

definitions.text: the curse of the drunk driver

indicators.note: throw out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and its s counts as a letter

explanation.surface: A pub chucking drinkers out early is the bane of those who drink and drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' rearranges the letters of THE BARS EARLY. This clue continues 14-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The police roadside breath-test device catches motorists who have been drinking, making it their bane.

clue.text: Nip nipper

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a small child

explanation.definitionFit: A small drink of liquor and a small child share the same short word.

clue.text: Pull girl up, as sluggish individual

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to drag is to pull
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: Hauling a young woman upward, as a slowcoach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns the whole of DRAGGAL round.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler who falls behind, a slowcoach.

clue.text: Carbon extracted from bit of dirt in shoe

indicators.note: extracted from means taken out, so the element's symbol is removed

parts.note: a scandal is a bit of dirt, a piece of gossip
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A lump of carbon has been dug out of the dirt in someone's shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirt' means gossip here: SCANDAL loses C.
explanation.definitionFit: An open summer shoe held on by straps.

clue.text: What 26 may be doing about one's work of art

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the participle goes round the numeral

parts.note: 26-across is a dog (in a pun), and a hot dog may be panting
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A creature from another clue panting around its own artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 26-across is HOT DOG; a hot dog would be PANTING, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made with oils or watercolours is a typical artwork.

clue.text: Elbow good naked?

annotationWithheld.why: Elbow good naked? (5): NUDGE is G (good) inside NUDE (naked), but no clue word signals the container; the only parse needs an implied indicator

clue.text: Bar bothering other houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A pub annoying neighbouring establishments.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'botherING OTher'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of metal such as gold is shaped like a bar.

clue.text: Marsupial's flap cut from behind

indicators.note: from behind means the letters are read starting at the end

parts.note: a tab is a small flap
to mow is to cut grass

explanation.surface: An Australian animal's pouch flap is snipped from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From behind' turns TABMOW round.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing Australian animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Snack stolen by setter, perhaps

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Food nicked by the compiler, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the crossword compiler but is the gun-dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage in a bread roll is a quick snack.

clue.text: Embraced by primate, bird starts to undo dress, showing talent

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the ape wraps around the rest

parts.note: an ape is a primate
a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: Hugged by an ape, a bird begins to undress, revealing a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes U and D from 'undo dress'; 'Embraced by' puts the bird and those letters inside the primate.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is a flair or gift for something.

clue.text: Shown to be attending Lord's, perhaps, my boss

parts.note: at means present at, attending
Lord's is the London cricket ground that hosts Test matches
ED is short for editor, the setter's boss

explanation.surface: Proved to be at Lord's watching cricket, says my employer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground where Test matches are played; the setter's boss is the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrated or confirmed as true by evidence.

clue.text: Lean on artist scarcely ever

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word for lean follows the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to rely on is to lean on

explanation.surface: Depending on a painter almost never.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the word for lean after the artist; a Royal Academician is a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom, infrequently.
